questions.stem: What happens when copper sulfate solution is electrolysed using copper electrodes?

options.text: Both electrodes dissolve into the solution
Hydrogen is produced at the cathode and oxygen at the anode
Copper deposits at the cathode and the copper anode dissolves, keeping the solution concentration constant
The solution turns from blue to green

questions.explanation: With copper electrodes, copper is deposited at the cathode (Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu) while the copper anode dissolves (Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻). Copper transfers from the anode to the cathode. The anode gets smaller, the cathode gets bigger, and the concentration of copper sulfate solution stays constant. This process is used for purifying copper.
